item.title: Fire spreads from barn to barn despite firefighters' efforts
item.description: Fire departments from Ash Grove, Walnut Grove, Willard, Dadeville, and Ebeneezer joined together to battle a barn fire that quickly spread to a second barn, but were unable to save the barns, though no animals or personnel were injured.

item.title: Snow to continue falling into Sunday morning

item.title: City Utilities provides tips to lower your winter bill and ease demand
item.description: City Utilities encourages customers to take simple steps to lower their winter bill and ease demand, such as setting their thermostat to 68°F, delaying major energy-consuming activities, limiting non-essential appliances and electronics, and minimizing heating and lighting in empty rooms.

item.title: Joey's Frozen Custard's barn catches fire
item.description: Firefighters responded to a barn fire at Joey's Frozen Custard in Seymour, and all animals were safely evacuated.

item.title: Highway Patrol Reports Hundreds of Calls as Winter Storm Sweeps Missouri
item.description: The Missouri State Highway Patrol responded to hundreds of incidents Saturday due to a winter storm, resulting in 601 calls for service, 78 stranded motorists, 100 non-injury crashes, 20 injury crashes, and one fatal crash.

item.title: Springfield woman hospitalized after aiming gun at deputy
item.description: A woman was hospitalized after pointing a gun at a sheriff's deputy during a well-being check, who then fired his firearm and hit her.

item.title: Winter Storm Slows Business Across Springfield as Some Stores Stay Open
item.description: Despite the winter storm, some businesses in Springfield are staying open to serve customers, while others are closing early due to slow traffic and dangerous roads.

item.title: Tips for drivers ahead of winter storm
item.description: SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — As winter weather approaches, Tim Fess, general manager at Rick's Automotive, reminds drivers to perform essential vehicle checks to ensure safety on the roads this weekend. item.title: List of warming centers for impending winter storm
item.description: Warming centers and cold weather shelters are opening up across the Ozarks due to forecasted freezing temperatures and negative wind chills, with a list of shelters and warming centers available on the CPO website and the Missouri Department of Health & Senior Services website.
